subject: Biology
title: Excretory Products and Their Elimination
summary: Animals excrete nitrogenous waste as ammonia (ammonotelic — most toxic, needs much water), urea (ureotelic) or uric acid (uricotelic — least toxic, little water).
Humans have a pair of kidneys, each with about one million nephrons. A nephron has a glomerulus and Bowman's capsule (Malpighian body) and a tubule: PCT, loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct.
Urine forms by glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption and secretion. The counter-current mechanism (loop of Henle + vasa recta) concentrates urine.
Kidney function is regulated by ADH, the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system and ANF. Lungs, liver and skin also help excretion.

formulas.name: Modes of excretion
formulas.formula: ammonotelic: bony fish, aquatic amphibians, aquatic insects;  ureotelic: mammals, many terrestrial amphibians, marine fish;  uricotelic: reptiles, birds, land snails, insects

formulas.name: Excretory structures
formulas.formula: protonephridia/flame cells (Platyhelminthes, Amphioxus);  nephridia (annelids);  Malpighian tubules (insects);  antennal/green glands (prawns);  kidneys (vertebrates)

formulas.name: Glomerular filtration rate
formulas.formula: GFR ≈ 125 mL/min ≈ 180 L/day;  urine ≈ 1–1.5 L/day → ~99% of filtrate is reabsorbed

formulas.name: Filtration membrane
formulas.formula: endothelium of glomerular blood vessels + basement membrane + epithelium of Bowman's capsule (podocytes with filtration slits)
formulas.when: Ultrafiltration — everything except proteins and cells passes.

formulas.name: Tubule functions
formulas.formula: PCT: reabsorbs 70–80% of electrolytes and water, all glucose and amino acids; secretes H⁺, NH₃, K⁺ (pH balance);  descending limb: permeable to water, not electrolytes;  ascending limb: impermeable to water, transports electrolytes;  DCT: conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, HCO₃⁻ reabsorption;  collecting duct: large water reabsorption, allows some urea to pass into the medulla

formulas.name: Counter-current mechanism
formulas.formula: opposite flow in limbs of Henle's loop and vasa recta → medullary osmolarity rises from 300 to about 1200 mOsmolL⁻¹ (NaCl + urea)
formulas.note: Human urine can be nearly four times more concentrated than the filtrate.

formulas.name: ADH (vasopressin)
formulas.formula: released from neurohypophysis when body fluid volume falls → more water reabsorbed from DCT and collecting duct;  deficiency → diabetes insipidus

formulas.name: RAAS
formulas.formula: low GFR/BP → JGA releases renin → angiotensinogen → angiotensin I → (ACE) angiotensin II (vasoconstrictor) → aldosterone from adrenal cortex → Na⁺ and water reabsorption → BP and GFR rise

formulas.name: ANF (atrial natriuretic factor)
formulas.formula: released when blood pressure/volume rises → vasodilation → lowers BP;  acts as a check on RAAS

formulas.name: Micturition
formulas.formula: urinary bladder stretches → stretch receptors → CNS → contraction of bladder smooth muscle and relaxation of urethral sphincter (micturition reflex)

formulas.name: Abnormal urine tests
formulas.formula: glycosuria (glucose) and ketonuria (ketone bodies) indicate diabetes mellitus

formulas.name: Disorders
formulas.formula: uremia (urea builds up — treated by haemodialysis);  renal calculi (kidney stones — crystallised salts, oxalates);  glomerulonephritis (inflammation of glomeruli)

examples.title: Filtrate per day
examples.problem: GFR is 125 mL/min. How much filtrate forms per day?

examples.title: Percentage reabsorbed
examples.problem: If 1.5 L urine is made from 180 L filtrate, what percentage is reabsorbed?

examples.title: Birds and uric acid
examples.problem: Why do birds excrete uric acid?
examples.solution: Uric acid is the least toxic and can be excreted as a paste with very little water, saving water and weight — useful for flying animals and for embryos inside shelled eggs.

examples.title: Diabetes insipidus
examples.problem: A person passes very large amounts of dilute urine with no glucose in it. Likely cause?
examples.solution: Lack of ADH (diabetes insipidus): without ADH, water is not reabsorbed from DCT and collecting ducts.

examples.title: Juxta medullary nephrons
examples.problem: Which nephrons have a long loop of Henle, and why does it matter?
examples.solution: Juxta medullary nephrons — their long loops run deep into the medulla and, with the vasa recta, build the medullary gradient needed for concentrated urine. Cortical nephrons have short loops.

examples.title: Haemodialysis
examples.problem: How does an artificial kidney work?
examples.solution: Blood from an artery is cooled, mixed with heparin (anticoagulant) and passed through a dialyser with cellophane tubes in a dialysing fluid like plasma but without nitrogenous wastes; wastes diffuse out and clean blood returns via a vein, with anti-heparin added.

topics.title: Human excretory system
topics.explain: Two kidneys, two ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra. Kidneys are reddish-brown, bean-shaped, about 10–12 cm long, 5–7 cm wide, 2–3 cm thick, 120–170 g; at the hilum the ureter, blood vessels and nerves enter or leave. Outer cortex, inner medulla with medullary pyramids; renal columns (columns of Bertini) are cortical extensions.

topics.title: Nephron structure
topics.explain: Glomerulus: tuft of capillaries formed by the afferent arteriole and drained by the efferent arteriole. Efferent arteriole forms the peritubular capillaries; a minute vessel running parallel to Henle's loop is the vasa recta (reduced or absent in cortical nephrons).

topics.title: Juxta glomerular apparatus (JGA)
topics.explain: A special sensitive region formed by cellular modification in the DCT and afferent arteriole where they contact. It senses a fall in GFR and releases renin.

topics.title: Role of other organs
topics.explain: Lungs remove about 200 mL CO₂ per minute and water. Liver secretes bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins and drugs in bile. Skin: sweat glands remove NaCl, small amounts of urea and lactic acid (mainly for cooling); sebaceous glands remove sterols, hydrocarbons and waxes.

topics.title: Kidney transplantation
topics.explain: The ultimate treatment for acute renal failure; a functioning kidney is taken from a donor, preferably a close relative, to reduce rejection by the immune system.

topics.title: Urine characteristics
topics.explain: Light yellow, watery, slightly acidic (pH 6.0); about 25–30 g urea excreted per day on average.

ratta: Ammonia: bony fish;  urea: mammals;  uric acid: birds, reptiles, insects.
PCT: all glucose & amino acids;  ascending limb impermeable to water.
ADH ↑ water reabsorption; lack → diabetes insipidus.
